text:
Please help me write our investor update for the half year. We make sensors that sit inside beehives and tell commercial beekeepers when a colony is weak, so they can treat it before it dies. We're raising a $600,000 bridge round and I want our current investors in it.

Where we are:
- We have 31 paying beekeepers. A year ago we had 12.
- Each sensor costs us $38 to make and we sell it for $55, plus $4 a month per hive for the app.
- Revenue for the last six months was $212,000. 70% of it came in March and April, before pollination season.
- Our biggest customer runs 4,000 hives and lost 18% of his colonies over the winter, against 31% the winter before. He says the sensors were part of it, but he also changed his mite treatment.
- We spend about $95,000 a month and have $340,000 left.
- A large farm equipment company launched a similar sensor in May at $45.

I want the update to say we'll be profitable next year. Keep it under 600 words.

Before I draft, there are a few things to settle. The main one is the profitability line.

**How the argument is built**

- **Claim:** Put $600k into the bridge, because it gets us to profitability.
- **Grounds:** Customers went from 12 to 31 in a year. Each sensor earns $17 over its cost, plus $4 a month per hive. Your biggest customer's winter losses fell from 31% to 18%.
- **Warrant:** A product that customers are adopting fast and that makes money on each unit will cover its costs once volume is high enough.
- **Weak points investors will see:** You spend about 2.7 times what you bring in. The cash runs out soon. A bigger competitor is now selling for less than you. And the 18% result comes from one customer who also changed his mite treatment.

**What your numbers show**

- **Spending vs. revenue:** You spend about $570k every six months and brought in $212k.
- **Runway:** Off-season revenue is roughly $16k a month (the 30% outside March and April). That puts net burn near $79k a month, so $340k lasts about four months. You'd run out around March, just before your selling season. That's the strongest reason for the bridge, and investors will work it out themselves.
- **Competitor:** Their $45 price is only $7 above your cost to make a sensor. Matching it would cut your hardware margin from 31% to about 16%.
- **Biggest customer:** With the mite treatment change, this result shows the product *can* help. It can't yet carry "the sensors cut losses by 13 points."

**On "profitable next year"**

Nothing you've given me so far supports it. You'd need roughly three times the revenue while a rival undercuts your price. Investors who already know your history will check this first. Two options:

1. **The flat version:** "We'll be profitable next year." This only holds if you have a plan with numbers I don't have yet.
2. **A conditional version:** "We break even at X hives on subscription. We're at Y. After the spring 2027 season we'll report where we are, and if we're short we'll do Z." As a rough guide: if subscriptions cost you almost nothing to deliver, $95k a month means about 24,000 hives on subscription, before counting what you make on hardware. Your real X depends on question 1 below.

It's your decision. I'd recommend option 2 unless you can give me the numbers behind option 1.

**Questions (most important first)**

1. **What does the $95k a month include, and how many hives are paying the $4 subscription now?** Is the cost of making sensors in the $95k or separate? Recurring revenue is the number investors will value most.
2. **What is your path to profitability?** Target customers, hives, price or cost cuts, and a date and number you're willing to be held to.
3. **The competitor:** have you lost any deals or customers since May? What do you have that they don't (accuracy, data, support, results)? This is the objection investors will raise first.
4. **Biggest customer:** what share of your revenue is he? Is he renewing? Do any other customers have before-and-after loss figures?
5. **The bridge terms:** what kind of investment it is (for example a SAFE or convertible note) and its cap or discount, the closing date, how much is already committed, and what milestone the $600k gets you to.
6. **Is there anything investors know or will find out** that isn't in your list? For example, an earlier forecast you missed, or customers who left.

Also: which six months does this cover? It's November now, but most of the revenue came in March and April, so the period matters for the runway figures. And who signs the update?

You're right, I can't promise profit next year. Go with option 2.

1. I don't know the breakdown of the $95k or how many hives are on the subscription right now.
2. I don't have a full path with numbers. What I can commit to is bringing spending down to $75k a month by February by not filling two open roles.
3. Their sensor only measures temperature. Ours also measures sound and hive weight. I don't know of any lost deals, but three of our beekeepers have asked to test their sensor.
4. I don't know his share of revenue, whether he's renewing, or whether other customers have before-and-after numbers.
5. It's a convertible note with a 20% discount and a $6M cap. It closes December 15. One angel has already committed $250k. I don't know what milestone to tie the $600k to. Investors who want in should reply to me by December 1.
6. Nothing else that I know of.

I'm not sure of the exact six months, so I'd have to check. I'll sign it.

I've written the update with the conditional version. It doesn't promise profit next year. Instead it commits to cutting spending to $75k a month by February and to sending investors a report after the spring 2027 season.

<final_document>
Subject: Half-year update and our $600,000 bridge round

Hi all,

This is where we stand after the last six months, and what we're asking of you.

**The short version**

We're raising a $600,000 bridge round on a convertible note with a 20% discount and a $6M cap. One angel has already committed $250,000, and we'd like the remaining $350,000 to come from you. If you want in, please reply to me by December 1. The round closes December 15.

**What's working**

- 31 commercial beekeepers now pay us, up from 12 a year ago.
- We make money on every sensor. Each one costs $38 to make and sells for $55. Each hive also pays $4 a month for the app.
- Revenue for the last six months was $212,000.
- Our largest customer runs 4,000 hives. He lost 18% of his colonies last winter, down from 31% the winter before. He says the sensors were part of that. He also changed his mite treatment, so we can't claim the whole drop. But it's the result our customers buy us for.

**What's hard**

- We spend about $95,000 a month, well more than we bring in, and we have $340,000 in the bank.
- Our revenue is seasonal. 70% of the last six months' revenue came in March and April, before pollination season. For most of the year we spend more than we earn.
- In May a large farm equipment company launched a competing sensor at $45. Theirs measures only temperature. Ours also measures sound and hive weight. We don't know of any deals lost to them, but three of our beekeepers have asked to test their sensor.

**What we're doing about it**

We will bring spending down to $75,000 a month by February by not filling two open roles.

I'm not going to promise you profitability next year. I don't yet have numbers solid enough to stand behind that. After the 2027 spring season, I'll send you a report on how many hives we're covering, what we sold and what that means for when we break even.

**Why the bridge, and why now**

Without it, our cash runs out around March, even after the spending cut and before counting any revenue. March is when the season that brings in most of our sales begins.

With the bridge we'd have about $940,000. At the lower spending level, that carries us through the 2027 season and into late 2027 before counting any revenue. That gives us a full selling season to show that beekeepers choose us over a cheaper rival, and to give you real numbers on the path to break-even.

You've backed us from 12 beekeepers to 31. I'd like you with us for the next season. If you have questions before you decide, reply or call me.

Thank you,

</final_document>

Things to check before you send it:

- **The six-month period.** The update just says "the last six months" for now. Once you've checked which months they were, put the dates in. If March and April fall outside them, the seasonality line needs to change.
- **Runway figures.** I worked these out myself, assuming you spend $95k a month until February and $75k after:
  - Without the bridge, cash runs out around mid-March.
  - With it, you have about $940k, which lasts to roughly November 2027.
  - Neither figure counts revenue, so both are conservative.
- **Signature.** I left the space after "Thank you," for your name.
- **Worth adding if you can get them in time:**
  - How many hives are paying the subscription now. Investors will value that recurring revenue most.
  - A break-even hive count.
  - A milestone for the $600k.
  - Whether your largest customer is renewing.

  Any one of these would make the case stronger. The update is about 470 words, so there's room.
